notes.title: SiamCTC:  Learning Speech Representations through Monotonic Temporal Alignment
notes.bp: A speech representation should recognize the same linguistic content when the speaker talks faster or slower.
notes.wh: Two views can have different frame counts, so frame-to-frame equality treats timing variation as content change.
notes.naive: Align every augmented frame to its counterpart and penalize harmless shifts.
notes.ap: Use CTC to learn a flexible monotonic alignment between views inside a Siamese learner.
notes.mech: Two encoders produce sequences and CTC sums over valid monotonic paths while training the representations to agree at content level.
notes.math: A monotonic path preserves temporal order while allowing variable durations; it is a soft alignment over possible boundaries.
notes.eval: A monotonic path preserves temporal order while allowing variable durations; it is a soft alignment over possible boundaries.
notes.ww: SiamCTC improves representation robustness at diverse speaking rates in the reported experiments.
notes.limits: Augmentation, language, CTC targets, downstream tasks, and rate range bound transfer; robustness is not universal recognition accuracy.
notes.evidence_boundary: D3 structured analyst note backed by captured PDF/text; result remains author-reported and was not independently reproduced.

notes.title: VoiceNet: Multilingual On-Device Phoneme-To-Audio Alignment
notes.bp: An avatar or speech tool needs phoneme boundaries quickly on-device, sometimes without a transcript and across languages.
notes.wh: Recognition and alignment must share computation, multilingual phonetics vary, and mobile latency limits model size.
notes.naive: Run a large offline aligner or require text and a separate recognizer before placing boundaries.
notes.ap: Train an end-to-end model for phoneme recognition and text-independent forced alignment, with optional text conditioning.
notes.mech: VoiceNet predicts phoneme evidence and timing on-device; text adds a constraint when available, and device tests expose latency.
notes.math: Alignment is ordered interval inference rather than a post-processing attachment to recognition.
notes.eval: Alignment is ordered interval inference rather than a post-processing attachment to recognition.
notes.ww: The paper reports competitive multilingual alignment and 6 ms average CPU phoneme inference on Galaxy devices.
notes.limits: Device, language, phoneme inventory, transcript availability, and splits bound transfer; latency is not alignment quality.
notes.evidence_boundary: D3 structured analyst note backed by captured PDF/text; result remains author-reported and was not independently reproduced.

notes.title: ZSDEVC: Zero-Shot Diffusion-based Emotional Voice Conversion with Disentangled Mechanism
notes.bp: Convert emotional expression for an unseen speaker while preserving words and recognizable identity.
notes.wh: Emotion and identity share acoustic cues, so changing one can distort content or impose training-speaker assumptions.
notes.naive: Train a speaker-specific converter or change prosody heuristically and accept identity leakage.
notes.ap: Use zero-shot diffusion with disentangled content, identity, and expressive guidance, testing unseen speakers in and out of domain.
notes.mech: Diffusion denoising reconstructs speech from a noisy latent while separate conditions guide emotion and speaker/content.
notes.math: Disentanglement asks emotion to move while content and identity remain stable enough for a listener.
notes.eval: Disentanglement asks emotion to move while content and identity remain stable enough for a listener.
notes.ww: The paper reports improved emotional accuracy and naturalness for unseen speakers across evaluated datasets.
notes.limits: Labels, speaker coverage, out-of-domain definition, protocol, and identity metrics bound transfer; conversion does not establish consent.
notes.evidence_boundary: D3 structured analyst note backed by captured PDF/text; result remains author-reported and was not independently reproduced.

notes.title: Private kNN-VC: Interpretable Anonymization of Converted Speech
notes.bp: An anonymizer should hide who spoke while keeping words and useful prosody, and evaluation should reveal what still identifies the person.
notes.wh: Prosody can leak identity after spectral conversion, while speaker recognition is only a privacy proxy.
notes.naive: Convert timbre alone and assume duration and pitch variation carry no identity information.
notes.ap: Add interpretable kNN-VC components that anonymize phone duration and variation, then vary target-speaker selection.
notes.mech: The anonymizer changes duration and prosodic variation around phones; a recognition attack tests whether those factors predict identity.
notes.math: Privacy is decomposed into leakage channels instead of one opaque score.
notes.eval: Privacy is decomposed into leakage channels instead of one opaque score.
notes.ww: The added components increase privacy in the tested attack, and target selection changes measured privacy.
notes.limits: Attack, target pool, language, utility metric, and prosody definitions bound the result; attack reduction is not anonymity.
notes.evidence_boundary: D3 structured analyst note backed by captured PDF/text; result remains author-reported and was not independently reproduced.

notes.title: Efficient Trie-based Biasing using K-step Prediction for Rare Word Recognition
notes.bp: Rare names and terms should be recognized when they are not common in the vocabulary.
notes.wh: Trie biasing rewards a partial word before knowing whether the full word completes, then revokes rewards during beam search.
notes.naive: Add a fixed bonus to every matching prefix and pay the cost of undoing it when the hypothesis fails.
notes.ap: Train a K-step predictor to look ahead and estimate whether a rare word will complete, avoiding score revocation.
notes.mech: The decoder predicts future steps from a prefix; synthetic data fine-tunes Whisper so contextual biasing becomes learned look-ahead.
notes.math: The method replaces delayed correction with an approximate future-value estimate, trading learned prediction for simpler decoding.
notes.eval: The method replaces delayed correction with an approximate future-value estimate, trading learned prediction for simpler decoding.
notes.ww: On NSC Part 2, reported WER falls from 30.86% to 12.19% after 10 hours of synthetic-data fine-tuning.
notes.limits: Synthetic realism, rare-word list, decoder, beam settings, and WER denominator bound the claim.
notes.evidence_boundary: D3 structured analyst note backed by captured PDF/text; result remains author-reported and was not independently reproduced.

notes.title: Multilingual Query-by-Example KWS for Indian Languages using Transliteration
notes.bp: Query-by-example search should find a spoken term across Indian languages without one language-specific phoneme inventory.
notes.wh: Phoneme symbols and pronunciation conventions differ, while query and target need comparable representations.
notes.naive: Use one shared phoneme dictionary and assume posteriors mean the same thing across languages.
notes.ap: Use multilingual ASR character logits in a shared Devanagari transliteration space for query and target audio.
notes.mech: The ASR maps ten languages to transliterated characters; posterior sequences become retrieval features.
notes.math: Transliteration changes the shared unit from language-specific phonemes to a common script-level sequence representation.
notes.eval: Transliteration changes the shared unit from language-specific phonemes to a common script-level sequence representation.
notes.ww: The method raises reported MTWV from 0.015 to 0.504 on IndicSUPERB and exceeds the Marathi baseline.
notes.limits: Language, script, ASR errors, query duration, and splits constrain transfer; script unification is not translation.
notes.evidence_boundary: D3 structured analyst note backed by captured PDF/text; result remains author-reported and was not independently reproduced.

notes.title: Defending Speech-enabled LLMs Against Adversarial Jailbreak Threats
notes.bp: A speech-enabled LLM should refuse harmful requests even when an attacker uses the speech channel.
notes.wh: Speech adds transcription, acoustic, and modality-transfer attack surfaces, while harmful data are scarce.
notes.naive: Apply text-only safety tuning or assume speech inherits the text safety boundary.
notes.ap: Adversarially train with synthesized harmful and benign speech, then test strong white-box attacks and data ablations.
notes.mech: Speech-domain harmful examples change the model; training configurations vary and safety is measured under attacks.
notes.math: Robustness is response behavior under a threat model, not ordinary accuracy.
notes.eval: Robustness is response behavior under a threat model, not ordinary accuracy.
notes.ww: Four hours of harmful plus 150 hours of benign speech yields reported relative safety gains of 45–300% over baseline.
notes.limits: Attack family, harm taxonomy, model, synthesis, and rubric bound the claim; refusal is not complete security.
notes.evidence_boundary: D3 structured analyst note backed by captured PDF/text; result remains author-reported and was not independently reproduced.

notes.title: Unfolding A Few Structures for The Many: Memory-Efficient Compression of Conformer and Speech Foundation Models
notes.bp: A speech model should fit memory and storage limits without losing larger-model behavior at different deployment depths.
notes.wh: Depth-specific models duplicate parameters, while compression can reduce capacity or make one operating point brittle.
notes.naive: Store a separate full model for each depth, or prune once and accept a fixed quality/resource tradeoff.
notes.ap: Train a compact seed and unfold it through shared structures, using KL self-distillation between largest and seed paths.
notes.mech: Logical depth changes through repeated blocks sharing a seed; distillation aligns small and large outputs across paths.
notes.math: Unfolding trades parameter storage for repeated computation, while KL divergence keeps paths behaviorally close.
notes.eval: Unfolding trades parameter storage for repeated computation, while KL divergence keeps paths behaviorally close.
notes.ww: The models report comparable ASR with 35% Conformer and 30% wav2vec2/HuBERT parameter reductions.
notes.limits: Hardware latency, unfolding cost, family, task, and benchmark coverage bound transfer; fewer parameters is not automatically less energy.
notes.evidence_boundary: D3 structured analyst note backed by captured PDF/text; result remains author-reported and was not independently reproduced.
